notes: Covers the main cases: names are added to the automate loader, global defaults reach them, internal names get the internal issuer, and existing site policies are reused; but it creates empty per-name policies even with no global options, gives internal names the global key_type unlike the reference, and rewrites site policies to add an explicit internal issuer, so the hidden output test fails.

A compact implementation that reuses forcedAutomatedNames for the loader, normalizes names like site addresses and makes an implicit internal issuer explicit (which helps the auto_https-off case); it fails the hidden test, it also edits site policies and does not account for internalAP overlap, and it has very thorough parser and adapt tests.

Closest to the reference in structure: it checks every existing policy, including the internal one, and leaves site policies untouched; but it always creates a policy (empty, noisy ones when there are no global options) and builds internal-name policies from the global base, so the adapted output diverges and the hidden test fails, though the tests are extensive and include a caddyfile adapt file.

A clean per-name policy approach placed after internalAP that never touches existing site or hostless policies, closely matching the reference semantics; it fails the hidden test, likely because of output differences such as extra subject-only policies when no global options are set and key_type carried on internal-name policies, but its tests are excellent (equivalence with a dummy site across many option sets plus a caddyfile_adapt fixture).

Handles the main example and no-site cases, but the logic is convoluted: it only knows about site-block names, ignoring the automate-loader and internal-policy names, so overlapping policies are possible; it rewrites site policies, sorts subjects, always creates base policies, and has fewer tests.

Covers the required behaviours (append parsing, policies without sites, internal/public split, site precedence, automate loader), but it fails the hidden test, the logic is convoluted (a separate siteAutomationNames map, two blocks reading the option, nested fix-ups of site policies), it emits subject-only empty policies the reference avoids, and the parser does not reject a trailing block.
